 J U D G M E N T

This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P(MV) No. 170 of 2012 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Muvattupuzha, dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
The respondents herein were the respondents before the Tribunal.

2. The case of the claimant is that, on 25.12.2011, while the claimant was riding his motorcycle bearing reg. no. KL-40/C 3595, along Perumbavoor-Moovattupuzha MC Road, a Tata Sumo bearing reg. no. KL-9/U 4950, driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on his motorcycle and thereby he suffered severe injuries including amputation of his right leg below the knee.
The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 10,00,000/-.
3. The 1st respondent was the owner-cum-driver and the 2nd respondent was the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Before the Tribunal, the 1st respondent remained 2026:KER:12739 MACA NO.
2486 OF 2015 ex-parte.
The 2nd respondent filed a written statement admitting the insurance policy but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed and denying the liability.
Exts. A1
to A9 and C1
were marked.

The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 6,97,900/- as compensation under different heads with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant had come up in appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondents.
5.

The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads :-
Notional income :-

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 8,000 was claimed, the Tribunal had taken only an amount of 4,500/-
as the monthly income of the injured who was a mason by profession.

It is further submitted that, even going by the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], 2026:KER:12739 MACA NO. 2486 OF 2015 the income of a Coolie, for an accident in 2011, is fixed as 8,000/-
and sought for enhancement of the income fixed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Following the judgment in Ramachandrappa (supra) and also considering the fact that the injured was a mason,
I find it appropriate to refix the monthly income as 8,000/-.
Loss of earnings:- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that towards loss of earnings, the Tribunal had taken the income of 10 months' period.

Since the monthly income is refixed at 8,000/-, the total compensation payable under the head is recalculated as:
Rajeev vs Prakasan on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58704234/
2 80,000/- (8000 x 10).
Since the Tribunal has only awarded an amount of 45,000/-, there will be an additional amount of 35,000/- under the head loss of earnings.
Compensation for pain and sufferings :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 40,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.
The claimant sustained serious injuries including amputation of the right leg below the knee.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the 2026:KER:12739 MACA NO. 2486 OF 2015 claimant, I find that a total amount of 1,00,000/- can be awarded under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 60,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.
Compensation for loss of amenities in life:-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has granted an amount of 30,000/- under the said head.
Considering the age of the claimant and the loss of enjoyment in life, I am inclined to grant 1,00,000/- under this head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 70,000/- under the head loss of amenities.
Extra nourishment :-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has granted only an amount of 1,500/- under the said head.
Considering that the claimant has undergone 15 days in-patient treatment, I am inclined to grant a consolidated amount of 3750/- under the afore head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 2,250/- under the head extra nourishment.
Bystander expenses:-
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has granted only an 2026:KER:12739 MACA NO. 2486 OF 2015 amount of 2,250/- under the said head.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, I am inclined to grant a consolidated amount of 15,000/- under the afore head.

Thus,
there will be an additional amount of 12,750/- under the head bystander expenses.

Compensation for continuing or permanent disability :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the right leg was amputated below the knee and in Ext.C1 certificate, permanent disability was assessed as 40%.
The learned Standing Counsel further submitted that though the assessment was not full body disability, the tribunal has taken 40% as permanent disability, which is on the higher side.
On a perusal of the Workmen's Compensation Act, it is seen that the percentage of functional disability of a person whose leg was amputated below the knee is taken as 50%.
Hence, in the present case, since there is amputation of the leg, I am inclined to take functional disability as 50%.

Since the functional disability of the claimant aged 31 years, is fixed as 50%, following National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors [2017 2026:KER:12739 MACA NO. 2486 OF 2015 (4) KLT 662 (SC)], by adding 40%
future prospects to the income fixed, 11,200 (8000 + 8000 x 40%) is the income for awarding compensation for permanent disability.

Accordingly, following Pranay Sethi (supra) and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)], the total compensation payable under the head permanent disability is recalculated as (11200 x 12 x 16 x 50/100) 10,75,200/- as the total compensation payable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since,
the Tribunal has awarded an amount of 3,67,200/- under the said head, there will be an additional amount of 7,08,000/- under the head permanent disability.
Compensation for future treatment/purchase of medicines:
On a perusal of the award, it is seen that no amount was granted by the Tribunal towards future treatment and for purchase of prosthesis.
The injured was aged only 31 years at the time of the accident and there is an amputation of right leg below knee
, hence I find it appropriate to award 5,00,000/- towards future treatment/purchase of prosthesis.
No document has been produced by the appellant to prove purchase of 2026:KER:12739 MACA NO. 2486 OF 2015 prosthesis.
However, considering the amputation of the leg, I am inclined to award an amount of 5,00,000/- towards purchase of prosthesis.
However, the interest for the afore amount will be only from the date of award.

6. Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.
Since the appeal is of the year 2015, I find it appropriate to fix the interest @ 7% per annum on the enhanced amount.
7. Thus, the impugned award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:-

By-stander expenses 10,000 2,250 12,750 15,000 5 Extra nourishment 10,000 1,500 2,250 3,750 charges 6 Transportation 10,000 1,500 Nil 1,500 charges 2026:KER:12739 MACA NO. 2486 OF 2015
7 Medical treatment 1,00,000 2,10,398 Nil 2,10,398 charges
8 Compensation for 4,00,000 3,67,200 7,08,000 10,75,200 permanent disability 9 Compensation for - Nil 5,00,000 5,00,000 future treatment/purchase of medicines 10,00,0000 6,97,848 13,88,000 20,85,848

TOTAL Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and the appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of 13,88,000/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakh Eighty Eight Thousand) over and above the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
The additional compensation awarded in appeal, except the amount of 5,00,000/- towards future treatment/medical expenses, will carry interest @7% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The amount of 5,00,000/- awarded towards future treatment/purchase of prosthesis will carry interest @ 7% per annum from the date of the award till realization and proportionate costs.

The respondent/insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this Rajeev vs Prakasan on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58704234/
4 judgment.

The appellant/claimant 2026:KER:12739 MACA NO. 2486 OF 2015 shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent/insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the respondent/insurer to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the respondent/insurer to deposit the said amount before the Tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest in accordance with law.
